turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Absolutely, that's an interesting question! When we listen to speech, our brains are remarkable at recognizing words, even if they're not pronounced perfectly. This is due to a process called phoneme restoration, where our brains fill in the gaps based on context and prior knowledge. So, if someone said 'strobe-ree' instead of 'straw-berry', your brain would likely still recognize it as a word, even though it's not spelled correctly. However, it's important to note that this process can sometimes lead to misunderstandings in conversation. In terms of psychology, this shows how our brains use complex strategies to make sense of the world around us.
